## What you'll learn

This tutorial uses the package's synthetic raw standards and unknown-sample datasets to show how to process signals, fit and inspect a conventional calibration, save it, and apply it to other samples. The shipped values support a reproducible example; they do not qualify an instrument or method.

## Prerequisites

- Basic R knowledge (data frames, pipes)
- Completed the [Getting Started](getting-started.html) tutorial
- Understanding of what SEC/GPC does (separates polymers by size)

## Example workflow

The first part processes twelve synthetic polystyrene standards and saves the fitted calibration. The second part applies that calibration to synthetic unknown chromatograms and compares calculated averages with the generator-assigned values in the example dataset.

## Setup

```{r setup}
library(measure)
library(measure.sec)
library(recipes)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

---

## Build the calibration

### Load raw standard data

The package includes `sec_raw_standards`, a synthetic tutorial dataset with twelve polystyrene standard traces. It was generated with noise, baseline drift, and injection artifacts to resemble features found in raw exports; it is not instrument data.

This example has three different kinds of values. `mp` is the molecular-weight
input used by the generator to place a standard peak. The generator's declared
retention-time convention is `19 - 0.75 * log10(mp)`; it is a construction
parameter, not a measurement. The raw maximum and the maximum after baseline
correction are observations extracted from the distributed traces. Treating
the generator input as if it were an independently measured peak would hide
the distinction this tutorial is intended to inspect.

```{r load-standards}
data(sec_raw_standards)

# View the structure - this is raw detector output
glimpse(sec_raw_standards)

# View the available standards
sec_raw_standards |>
  distinct(standard_name, mp, log_mp, dispersity) |>
  arrange(desc(mp)) |>
  print(n = 12)
```

```{r plot-raw-standards, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="Three synthetic raw RI traces selected from the standard set to span its molecular-weight range. Each panel uses its own signal range and shows the noise and baseline variation present in the tutorial data.", fig.alt="Three-panel faceted line chart of synthetic raw RI signals for PS-580, PS-67500, and PS-930000. Elution time in minutes is on the horizontal axis and raw RI signal in millivolts is on the vertical axis. The named standards' peaks occur at earlier times for higher molecular weights; each panel uses a separate vertical scale."}
sec_raw_standards |>
  filter(standard_name %in% c("PS-580", "PS-67500", "PS-930000")) |>
  arrange(standard_name, time_min) |>
  ggplot(aes(time_min, ri_mv)) +
  geom_line(color = "#2E86AB", linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(vars(standard_name), ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Elution time (min)",
    y = "RI signal (mV)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

Notice that:

- Higher MW standards elute earlier (larger molecules excluded from pores)
- Lower MW standards elute later (smaller molecules enter pores)
- There's visible noise and baseline variation—this is normal for raw data

### Process the standards

Before building a calibration curve, we need to:

1. Baseline correct each chromatogram
2. Find the peak retention time for each standard

```{r process-standards}
# Process each standard separately and find peak retention times
process_standard <- function(std_data) {
  std_name <- unique(std_data$standard_name)
  mp <- unique(std_data$mp)

  raw_peak_idx <- which.max(std_data$ri_mv)
  raw_retention_time <- std_data$time_min[[raw_peak_idx]]
  generator_retention_time <- 19 - 0.75 * log10(mp)

  # Create recipe for baseline correction
  rec <- recipe(ri_mv + time_min ~ standard_name, data = std_data) |>
    update_role(standard_name, new_role = "id") |>
    step_measure_input_long(
      ri_mv,
      location = vars(time_min),
      col_name = "ri"
    ) |>
    step_sec_baseline(measures = "ri")

  # Process
  processed <- prep(rec) |> bake(new_data = NULL)

  # Extract chromatogram data
  chrom <- processed$ri[[1]]

  # Find peak (maximum signal after baseline correction)
  peak_idx <- which.max(chrom$value)
  peak_time <- chrom$location[peak_idx]
  peak_height <- chrom$value[peak_idx]

  tibble(
    standard_name = std_name,
    mp = mp,
    log_mp = log10(mp),
    generator_retention_time = generator_retention_time,
    raw_retention_time = raw_retention_time,
    retention_time = peak_time,
    peak_height = peak_height
  )
}

# Process all standards
peak_data <- sec_raw_standards |>
  group_by(standard_name, mp) |>
  group_split() |>
  purrr::map(process_standard) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  arrange(desc(mp))

print(peak_data)
```

The following plot keeps the generator target beside the two peak locations
actually extracted from each trace. It is a diagnostic of this fixture, not a
calibration acceptance plot: noise, drift, peak shape, and the chosen baseline
window can move the observed maximum away from the generator input.

```{r compare-standard-apices, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="Declared generator peak times and two observed maxima for the twelve distributed synthetic standards. The generator time is the input convention; raw and baseline-corrected times are maxima extracted from the shipped traces.", fig.alt="Line plot on a logarithmic molecular-weight axis comparing declared generator peak time, raw detector maximum, and baseline-corrected detector maximum for twelve synthetic standards. Higher molecular weights have earlier nominal times, while several raw and corrected maxima depart from the declared times."}
apex_comparison <- peak_data |>
  select(
    standard_name,
    mp,
    generator_retention_time,
    raw_retention_time,
    retention_time
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      generator_retention_time,
      raw_retention_time,
      retention_time
    ),
    names_to = "source",
    values_to = "retention_time"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    source = recode(
      source,
      generator_retention_time = "Generator input",
      raw_retention_time = "Raw maximum",
      retention_time = "Baseline-corrected maximum"
    )
  )

ggplot(apex_comparison, aes(mp, retention_time, color = source, shape = source)) +
  geom_line(
    aes(group = standard_name),
    color = "grey75",
    linewidth = 0.35,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 2.3) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(
    x = "Standard molecular weight input (Da)",
    y = "Peak time (min)",
    color = NULL,
    shape = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

The noiseless peaks elute in the expected order. Two neighboring pairs reverse
after noise is added; three reverse after baseline correction. For the 580 Da
standard, the raw maximum is at 17.015 minutes and the corrected maximum at
15.668 minutes. The final 5% of this trace still contains, on average, 63% of
the noiseless peak height. Subtracting that edge as background changes the
shape of the peak. The [fixture replay](https://github.com/JamesHWade/measure.sec/tree/main/tools/fixture-qualification)
shows the intermediate signals for all twelve standards.

### Build the calibration curve

Now we fit a polynomial relationship between retention time and log(MW):

```{r build-calibration}
# Prepare calibration data in the required format
cal_data <- peak_data |>
  select(standard_name, retention = retention_time, log_mw = log_mp)
ps_cal <- cal_data |> select(retention, log_mw)

# Fit a cubic polynomial for this workflow example
cal_fit <- lm(log_mw ~ poly(retention, 3, raw = TRUE), data = cal_data)

# View fit summary
summary(cal_fit)

# Calculate R-squared
cat("\nCalibration R² =", round(summary(cal_fit)$r.squared, 5), "\n")
```

```{r plot-calibration, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="Cubic calibration fitted to the peak retention times of the twelve synthetic standards. The shaded band is a 95% confidence interval for the fitted mean curve, not a prediction interval for a future measurement. The curve turns upward near both ends and departs substantially from several points in this example.", fig.alt="Scatter chart of twelve synthetic polystyrene standards with a cubic calibration curve and confidence band. Retention time in minutes is on the horizontal axis; log10 peak molecular weight in daltons is on the vertical axis. The cubic curve decreases through the middle and turns upward near both ends; several standards sit far from the fitted curve. The shaded band is the 95% confidence interval for the fitted mean."}
cal_pred <- cal_data |>
  mutate(
    fitted = predict(cal_fit),
    residual = log_mw - fitted
  )

cal_grid <- tibble(
  retention = seq(
    min(cal_data$retention),
    max(cal_data$retention),
    length.out = 200
  )
)
curve_interval <- predict(
  cal_fit,
  newdata = cal_grid,
  interval = "confidence",
  level = 0.95
)
cal_grid <- bind_cols(cal_grid, as_tibble(curve_interval))

ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = cal_grid,
    aes(retention, ymin = lwr, ymax = upr),
    fill = "#A23B72",
    alpha = 0.18
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = cal_grid,
    aes(retention, fit),
    color = "#A23B72",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = cal_pred,
    aes(retention, log_mw),
    size = 2.4,
    color = "#2E86AB"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Retention time (min)",
    y = expression(log[10](M[p] / Da)),
    title = "Cubic calibration from synthetic standards",
    subtitle = paste("R² =", round(summary(cal_fit)$r.squared, 5))
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

This synthetic fit is unsuitable for quantitative use: R-squared is about 0.832, the curve turns upward near both ends, and some standards have large percent differences. The unknown-sample comparison below also shows poor agreement. For an experimental run, inspect the standards and their baseline regions before interpreting any calculated molecular weights.

### Review calibration fit

Inspect the residuals for structure and compare predicted molecular weights with the declared `mp` inputs for each standard. R² and RMSE summarize the fit, but neither has a universal acceptance threshold; set criteria for the method and its intended use.

```{r validate-calibration, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap=c("Residuals from the cubic fit at the twelve synthetic standards. The horizontal line marks zero residual.", "Percent difference between fitted and declared peak molecular-weight inputs for each synthetic standard. The zero line marks agreement; no acceptance limits are shown."), fig.alt=c("Residual chart with retention time in minutes on the horizontal axis and residual in log10 peak molecular weight on the vertical axis. Points for twelve standards are connected to a zero reference line; their pattern shows where the cubic fit is above or below each declared input.", "Horizontal bar chart of percent difference from the declared peak molecular-weight input for twelve synthetic standards. Standard names are listed vertically and deviation is on the horizontal axis. A zero line marks exact agreement; bars extend to either side according to the signed difference.")}
# Calculate % deviation for each standard
cal_pred <- cal_pred |>
  left_join(peak_data |> select(standard_name, mp), by = "standard_name") |>
  mutate(
    predicted_mp = 10^fitted,
    pct_deviation = (predicted_mp - mp) / mp * 100
  )

# Residual plot
p1 <- ggplot(cal_pred, aes(retention, residual)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "#2E86AB") +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = retention, yend = 0), alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    x = "Retention time (min)",
    y = "Residual in log10(Mp / Da)",
    title = "Calibration residuals"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

# Percent deviation bar chart
p2 <- ggplot(cal_pred, aes(reorder(standard_name, mp), pct_deviation)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2E86AB") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Difference from declared Mp (%)",
    title = "Percent difference by standard"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

# Display plots
p1
p2
```

```{r calibration-summary}
# Calibration quality summary
cat("=== Calibration Quality Summary ===\n\n")
cat("R-squared:        ", round(summary(cal_fit)$r.squared, 6), "\n")
cat("Residual Std Err: ", round(summary(cal_fit)$sigma, 4), "log₁₀ MW\n")
cat("Max |% Deviation|:", round(max(abs(cal_pred$pct_deviation)), 2), "%\n")
cat("Mean |% Deviation|:", round(mean(abs(cal_pred$pct_deviation)), 2), "%\n")
cat("\nCalibration Range:\n")
cat("  MW:        ", format(min(peak_data$mp), big.mark = ","), "to",
    format(max(peak_data$mp), big.mark = ","), "Da\n")
cat("  Retention: ", round(min(cal_data$retention), 2), "to",
    round(max(cal_data$retention), 2), "min\n")
```

### Save the calibration

Save the fitted calibration object so later recipes can reuse it without fitting again. This example uses a synthetic PS-50K trace to prepare the step; `ps_cal` defines the calibration standards.

```{r prepare-calibration-for-save}
data(sec_triple_detect, package = "measure.sec")
calibration_trace <- sec_triple_detect |>
  filter(sample_id == "PS-50K")

calibration_recipe <- recipe(
  ri_signal + elution_time ~ sample_id,
  data = calibration_trace
) |>
  update_role(sample_id, new_role = "id") |>
  step_measure_input_long(
    ri_signal,
    location = vars(elution_time),
    col_name = "ri"
  ) |>
  step_sec_baseline(measures = "ri") |>
  step_sec_conventional_cal(
    measures = "ri",
    standards = ps_cal,
    fit_type = "cubic",
    extrapolation = "none"
  )

prepped_calibration <- prep(calibration_recipe)
```

```{r save-calibration}
# Use a temporary file here; replace it with a managed path in your workflow.
cal_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
save_sec_calibration(
  prepped_calibration,
  file = cal_file,
  metadata = list(
    date = Sys.Date(),
    column = "<column-id>",
    instrument = "<instrument-id>",
    mobile_phase = "<mobile-phase>",
    flow_rate = "<flow-rate>",
    temperature = "<temperature>"
  )
)
```

> Include the date and method details in the filename or metadata. Follow your method criteria to decide when to repeat calibration.

---

## Apply the calibration

### Load a saved calibration

```{r load-calibration}
# Load the calibration saved above
cal_saved <- load_sec_calibration(cal_file)

# View the metadata
stopifnot(
  !is.null(cal_saved$user_metadata$date),
  identical(cal_saved$user_metadata$column, "<column-id>")
)
cat("Calibration from:", as.character(cal_saved$user_metadata$date), "\n")
cat("Column:", cal_saved$user_metadata$column, "\n")
cat("Fit type:", cal_saved$fit_type, "\n")
```

The recipes use the saved calibration object. Its retention range also defines the integration window for the averages below.

```{r use-calibration}
calibration_range <- range(ps_cal$retention)
```

### Load unknown samples

For the five single-main-peak samples, the generator uses `true_mw` to place
the main peak and `true_dispersity` to set its width. It attaches `true_mn`
and `true_mz` as labels; the generated signals do not have to integrate to
those values. The bimodal sample has two assigned component masses.

```{r load-unknowns}
data(sec_raw_unknowns)

# View the samples
sec_raw_unknowns |>
  distinct(
    sample_id,
    description,
    true_mw,
    true_mn,
    true_mz,
    true_dispersity
  ) |>
  print()
```

```{r plot-unknowns, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="Synthetic raw RI chromatograms for the six generator-defined unknown samples. Each facet has an independent vertical scale so differences in trace shape remain visible.", fig.alt="Faceted line chart with six panels, one per synthetic unknown sample. Elution time in minutes is on the horizontal axis and raw RI signal in millivolts is on the vertical axis. The panels show the generator-defined trace shapes on separate vertical ranges; no sample identification or instrument conclusion is inferred from them."}
sec_raw_unknowns |>
  arrange(sample_id, time_min) |>
  ggplot(aes(time_min, ri_mv)) +
  geom_line(color = "#2E86AB", linewidth = 0.35) +
  facet_wrap(vars(sample_id), scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Elution time (min)",
    y = "RI signal (mV)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

All six traces run from 4 to 22 minutes. The measured standard maxima span
only 14.6367–16.2083 minutes. That interval contains 944 of 10,801 readings
per trace (8.7%). It accounts for 19.3%–23.0% of the positive, baseline-corrected
signal area, depending on the sample. Read those percentages as detector
response inside the window; they do not measure sample recovery.

### Analyze an unknown sample

Now we apply our calibration to calculate molecular weights. Each example integrates only the portion within the standards’ retention range; signal outside that range is excluded, so the reported values may not represent the entire sample.

```{r analyze-unknowns}
# Process all unknowns at once
# First, let's work with one sample to show the workflow
unknown_a <- sec_raw_unknowns |>
  filter(sample_id == "Unknown-A")

# Build the analysis recipe
rec_unknown <- recipe(ri_mv + time_min ~ sample_id, data = unknown_a) |>
  update_role(sample_id, new_role = "id") |>
  step_measure_input_long(
    ri_mv,
    location = vars(time_min),
    col_name = "ri"
  ) |>
  step_sec_baseline(measures = "ri") |>
  step_sec_conventional_cal(
    calibration = cal_saved,
    extrapolation = "none"
  ) |>
  step_sec_mw_averages(integration_range = calibration_range)

# Process
result_a <- prep(rec_unknown) |> bake(new_data = NULL)

# View results
result_a |>
  select(sample_id, mw_mn, mw_mw, mw_mz, mw_dispersity)
```

### Process the remaining unknowns

Process the remaining synthetic samples with the same recipe:

```{r analyze-all-unknowns}
analyze_unknown <- function(sample_data) {
  sample_id <- unique(sample_data$sample_id)

  rec <- recipe(ri_mv + time_min ~ sample_id, data = sample_data) |>
    update_role(sample_id, new_role = "id") |>
    step_measure_input_long(
      ri_mv,
      location = vars(time_min),
      col_name = "ri"
    ) |>
    step_sec_baseline(measures = "ri") |>
    step_sec_conventional_cal(
      calibration = cal_saved,
      extrapolation = "none"
    ) |>
    step_sec_mw_averages(integration_range = calibration_range)

  result <- prep(rec) |> bake(new_data = NULL)

  result |>
    select(sample_id, mw_mn, mw_mw, mw_mz, mw_dispersity)
}

# Analyze the non-bimodal samples in this example
all_results <- sec_raw_unknowns |>
  filter(sample_id != "Unknown-Bimodal") |>  # Skip bimodal for standard analysis
  group_by(sample_id) |>
  group_split() |>
  purrr::map(analyze_unknown) |>
  bind_rows()

print(all_results)
```

### Compare with the assigned values

Compare the moments calculated inside the calibrated window with the assigned
values for each sample. A large difference here cannot tell you whether an
instrument would recover the sample's molecular-weight distribution.

```{r validate-results}
# Join with generator-assigned values
validation <- all_results |>
  left_join(
    sec_raw_unknowns |>
      distinct(sample_id, true_mw, true_dispersity),
    by = "sample_id"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(true_mw)) |>
  mutate(
    mw_error_pct = (mw_mw - true_mw) / true_mw * 100,
    disp_error_pct = (mw_dispersity - true_dispersity) / true_dispersity * 100
  )

# Summary table
validation |>
  select(
    sample_id,
    `Calc Mw` = mw_mw,
    `Assigned Mw` = true_mw,
    `Mw Difference %` = mw_error_pct,
    `Calc Đ` = mw_dispersity,
    `Assigned Đ` = true_dispersity
  ) |>
  mutate(
    `Calc Mw` = round(`Calc Mw`),
    `Mw Difference %` = round(`Mw Difference %`, 1),
    `Calc Đ` = round(`Calc Đ`, 2)
  )
```

```{r validation-plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="Calculated and assigned generator weight-average molecular weights for the synthetic unknown samples, using only the measured portion within calibration support. The dashed identity line marks agreement; omitted signal outside the calibration range is not represented. The calculated values cluster near 130–141 kDa while assigned values span about 3.5 kDa to 1.5 MDa. The table above gives sample IDs.", fig.alt="Log-scale parity chart comparing assigned generator Mw on the horizontal axis with calculated Mw on the vertical axis, both in daltons. Five calculated values cluster near 130–141 thousand Da; the 125 thousand Da assignment is closest to the identity line. The dashed identity line marks agreement; most samples lie far from it. The table above identifies the samples."}
# Parity plot: calculated vs assigned values
parity_limits <- range(c(validation$true_mw, validation$mw_mw), finite = TRUE)

ggplot(validation, aes(true_mw, mw_mw)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  geom_point(size = 4, color = "#2E86AB") +
  scale_x_log10(limits = parity_limits, labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = parity_limits, labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(
    x = "Assigned generator Mw (Da)",
    y = "Calculated Mw (Da)",
    title = "Calculated and assigned Mw"
  ) +
  coord_equal(xlim = parity_limits, ylim = parity_limits) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

## Special case: bimodal signal

The synthetic `Unknown-Bimodal` trace is described as a mixture with generator-assigned component values of 50,000 and 200,000 Da. Molecular-weight averages summarize the calibrated portion of the trace; inspect the signal and support before interpreting components.

```{r bimodal, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="The synthetic bimodal trace is plotted against calibrated molecular weight only at measured locations with finite calibration values. Vertical guides mark the generator-assigned 50,000 and 200,000 Da component values; signal outside finite calibration support is omitted.", fig.alt="Point chart of baseline-corrected RI response against calibrated molecular weight in daltons on a logarithmic horizontal axis. The displayed points form a broad cloud over the finite sampled calibration support; vertical guides mark the generator-assigned 50,000 and 200,000 Da component values. No line joins points across omitted support."}
# Process bimodal sample
bimodal <- sec_raw_unknowns |>
  filter(sample_id == "Unknown-Bimodal")

rec_bimodal <- recipe(ri_mv + time_min ~ sample_id, data = bimodal) |>
  update_role(sample_id, new_role = "id") |>
  step_measure_input_long(
    ri_mv,
    location = vars(time_min),
    col_name = "ri"
  ) |>
  step_sec_baseline(measures = "ri") |>
  step_sec_conventional_cal(
    calibration = cal_saved,
    extrapolation = "none"
  ) |>
  step_sec_mw_averages(integration_range = calibration_range)

result_bimodal <- prep(rec_bimodal) |> bake(new_data = NULL)

cat("Bimodal sample results:\n")
cat("  Mn =", round(result_bimodal$mw_mn), "Da\n")
cat("  Mw =", round(result_bimodal$mw_mw), "Da\n")
cat("  Dispersity =", round(result_bimodal$mw_dispersity, 2), "\n")

# Pair RI response with calibrated MW at the exact measured location.
# Points avoid drawing a line across excluded calibration support.
ri_curve <- as.data.frame(result_bimodal$ri[[1]]) |>
  rename(ri_response = value)

mw_curve <- as.data.frame(result_bimodal$mw[[1]]) |>
  transmute(location, molecular_weight = 10^value)

bimodal_chrom <- ri_curve |>
  left_join(mw_curve, by = "location") |>
  filter(is.finite(molecular_weight), is.finite(ri_response))

ggplot(bimodal_chrom, aes(molecular_weight, ri_response)) +
  geom_point(color = "#2E86AB", size = 0.45, alpha = 0.65) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = c(50000, 200000),
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "#A23B72"
  ) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(
    x = "Calibrated molecular weight (Da)",
    y = "Baseline-corrected RI signal (mV)",
    title = "Synthetic bimodal sample",
    subtitle = "Vertical guides mark the two generator-assigned component values"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Possible Cause | Solution |
|---------|---------------|----------|
| MW values all NA | Retention times outside calibration range | Check supported locations; use standards that bracket the sample range |
| Very high error for HMW samples | Extrapolation beyond highest standard | Use higher MW standards or additional standards or a method validated for that range |
| Dispersity > 3 | Broad or multiple populations, integration, or baseline effects | Inspect the trace and method support before interpreting |
| Negative detector response | Low signal or baseline correction | Inspect raw and corrected signals; do not interpret a negative response as molecular weight |
| Inconsistent results day-to-day | Calibration drift | Rebuild calibration; check column condition |

## Summary

The code sequence demonstrates standard processing, calibration saving, application, and comparison with generator-assigned values. This synthetic example does not provide quantitative sample results.

### Key points

- **Choose standards**: Use suitable standards that bracket the molecular-weight range of interest
- **Review calibration fit**: Inspect residuals and compare deviations with method-specific criteria
- **Watch for extrapolation**: MW values outside your calibration range are unreliable
- **Save calibrations with metadata**: Include date, column, conditions for traceability
- **Set a recalibration schedule**: Follow your method and lab criteria; recheck calibration when the column, mobile phase, or system suitability changes
